title: Section calculus for the actual sheaf tensor and scalar extension
statement: For a commutative ring sheaf R on a small site, use the actual sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Define pure_R(m,n) as the sheafification-unit image of m tensor n followed by the inverse tensor/sheafification comparison. This is bilinear, commutes with restrictions, is natural in both modules, and determines linear maps out of the tensor. For c:A→B construct the sheafified extension-of-scalars functor T_c with objects changeOfRings c M, its restriction-of-scalars right adjoint, and their adjunction. Its underlying unit sends m to the sheafification image of 1 tensor m. Module sheafification is [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

proof.text: Construct the public scalar-extension functor sectionwise with ModuleCat.extendScalars, then compose with module sheafification. Combine the sectionwise extension/restriction Hom equivalences with the sheafification adjunction. Import all Sheaf.CategoryTheory.ModulePullbackPushforwardAdjunction and use its existing tensorRestriction_tmul and both tensorHomEquiv naturality theorems in the construction. Its existing tensorUnit_apply and tensorAdjunction_underlying supply the insertion and mate formulas directly in the scalar-comparison and final-assembly proofs; no duplicate statement is declared.

Define pure tensors using the actual sheafification unit and tensorObjIsoSheafification. Naturality of those maps gives restriction compatibility. The sheafification adjunction and sectionwise tensor induction prove extensionality. The two whiskering identities for tensorObjIsoSheafification give simultaneous naturality.
